text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Visiting Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro said that Italy supports without reservation Hungary's future membership in the EU and NATO. @
- Parliament opened a debate on Wednesday on compensation for Hungarian Jews and on amending the act on bankruptcy.

- New agricultural minister-designate Frigyes Nagy told Parliament's agricultural committee that until Hungary joins the European Union he does not support the idea of foreigners obtaining ownership of land.
- Mihaly Kokeny, nominee for the post of minister of welfare said that there would be a 13-14 per cent price increase for medicines next year. @
- The Budapest Metropolitan Court opened a hearing on a civil case on Wednesday launched by the State Privatisation and Holding Co. against lawyer Marta Tocsik.

- The cabinet is expected to hold consultations on the draft of a new pension system at its regular meeting today as well as tackling reports on debentures and the operation of a morgage credit institute.

- Slovak President Michal Kovac told the Slovak Parliament that ethnic Hungarians, due to the absence of an act on the use of minority languages, are justified in feeling restricted in exercise of their constitutional rights. @
- The Office for Fair Competition has approved the purchase by Danubius Hotels Rt. of an 85 percent stake in HungarHotels.

- The privatisation of the electricity and gas sector must be suspended immediately, since the privatisation methods applied over the last two years are causing irreparable damage, representatives of the independent Hungarian Energy Association claimed at their general assembly.

- Consumer prices went up by an average of 0.8 percent in November. Vilaggazdasag reports that energy consumer prices increased by an average of 22.6 percent between December 1995 and November 1996. @
- Arrabona Konzorcium, comprising 57 agricultural cooperatives in Western Hungary, has purchased a 74 percent stake in the spirits producer Gyori Szeszgyar.
NEPSZABADSAG

- Laszlo Bekesi, former Socialist finance minister, contacted members of the Socialist parliamentary group on Wednesday urging personnel changes in the cabinet, party leadership and parliamentary group leadership.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @
- The Romanian Foreign Ministry welcomed the ratification of the Hungarian-Romanian basic treaty by the Hungarian Parliament.
- Industrial production in October of this year increased by 3.8 percent from the previus month, showing a growth of 5.8 percent over October 1995.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. has awarded a stake in the sugar factory Kabai Cukorgyar to the Dutch company Eastern Sugar BV. @
- Credit Swiss First Boston has confirmed an offer to buy shares in the chemical giant TVK, following TVK's repurchase of an 11.6 percent package of its own shares.
- The Czech National Bank has approved the sale of Interbanka to a consortium comprising Bayerische Landesbank Girozentrale and its part-owned interest Magyar Kulkereskedelmi Bank.
- Two plant employees and three security guards systematically stole car components valued at HUF 27 million or more from the Suzuki plant in Esztergom.
